answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils with latency triangulation: each identity must answer timed challenges from beacons on three continents, and its round-trip delays form a spiral fingerprint of where it really sits. A farm running thousands of fakes from one server room returns near-identical timings, like timber stacked in a single yard, and is cut as one cluster. Spreading fakes worldwide costs real machines and bandwidth in every region, while one honest agent answers once, as lightly as a zephyr, and passes.
